info.title: Wildward API
info.description: Public catalogue and staff editorial API (R1). Population counts are strings (bigint). Staff routes need the session cookie; mutations also need Origin and x-csrf-token.

csrfToken.description: Send this back in the x-csrf-token header on every mutation. It is also set as a readable cookie.

status.description: Headline assessment: global if there is one, else regional; most recent first

regionCount.description: Number of countries, seas and oceans; null when locations are withheld

layer.description: range: a published range map is shown. country: only country/sea-level presence is known, so whole regions are shaded.

slug.description: Region slug; its shape is in GET /map/basemap

species.description: Slugs of the species shaded here

coordinates.description: WGS84 [longitude, latitude]; never crosses ±180 (shapes are split there)

generalized.description: True when the shape was generalized to whole countries or seas to protect the species

geometry.description: Clipped to the viewport and simplified for display

truncated.description: True when a species or vertex cap cut the result short; zoom in to see everything

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north]; west > east crosses the antimeridian

status.description: Headline assessment: global if there is one, else regional; most recent first

regionCount.description: Number of countries, seas and oceans; null when locations are withheld

occurrences.description: How the species occurs in this region, as the source records it

facets.description: Counts of published species in this region

assessmentIndex.description: Index into `assessments` of the same payload

datasetVersion.description: Version of the source dataset, if any

generalizationNote.description: How the shape was simplified. Set automatically for location-sensitive species.

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon, WGS84 [lon, lat], at most 50000 vertices. Longitudes may run to ±540 to cross the antimeridian in one shape; it is split at ±180 on save. For "generalize_country" species the shape is replaced by the whole countries (or seas) it covers; "hide_regions" species cannot have ranges.

locator.description: Page, table or section in the source

editorial.description: Editorial JSON, validated by the versioned zod schema

ranges.description: Published range maps (approved through the revision workflow)

editorial.description: Editorial JSON, validated by the versioned zod schema

ranges.description: Published range maps (approved through the revision workflow)

expectedUpdatedAt.description: updatedAt from your last read. A mismatch means someone else saved first (409).

notAssessed.description: Explicitly marked "Not assessed" by an editor

pointValue.description: Counts are decimal strings (bigint). null is "not stated", never zero.

locationWithheld.description: True when the species is location-sensitive and its regions are withheld

locationGeneralized.description: True when locations are shown only at whole-country (or sea) level to protect the species

ranges.description: Published range maps. Empty when only country-level presence is known.

domain.description: Destination domain, shown next to the link

credit.description: Credit as recorded when this revision was saved

license.description: Licence as recorded when this revision was saved

accessedOn.description: Date the source was accessed (import date)

reviewerRole.description: Role of the reviewer. Names are never published.

selfReviewed.description: True when the author published their own revision. Never presented as independent review.

related.description: Up to 4 published species sharing group, threats or (non-sensitive) regions

threatened.description: Published species whose headline category is CR, EN or VU

status.description: same_basis: every species has a wild, global, numeric estimate in one shared unit. Values are still never combined or scored.

reviewedAt.description: When site staff last reviewed this organization. A review is not a certification of effectiveness.
